export const meta = {
  name: 'heldout-diagnosis-and-simpl',
  description: 'Diagnose the held-out translator failures on Biamp and Clock Audio, and answer the SIMPL question against real .usp source',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Diagnose', detail: 'why the translator degrades out-of-sample; SIMPL+ source analysis' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial check per dimension' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'what generalises, what was overfit, what to do' },
  ],
}

const R = '/Users/robp/GitHub/rob-paprocki/extron-driver-convert'

const GROUND = `
PROJECT: ${R}. A .pkp -> ControlScript translator plus supporting tools, all tested.

THE HELD-OUT RESULT THAT PROMPTED THIS WORK. Until now every rule in tools/pkp2cs.py was both
DERIVED FROM and VALIDATED AGAINST the same four device pairs. That is circular. Two new
third-party families arrived with both a .pkp and its shipped ControlScript module, giving the
first genuine out-of-sample test. Run with no tuning whatsoever, the first honest numbers are:

  IN-SAMPLE (the four the rules were built on):
    DSC 12G-HD      28/29 commands wire-matching
    DTP3 CP 42      27/28
    Samsung serial   9/9
    Automate VX     17/18
    dangling self-calls across all five generated modules: 5

  HELD-OUT (never seen by any rule):
    Clock Audio clau_25_5940 (CDT100 MK3)    6 shared,  1 matching, 5 differing, 0 dangling
    Clock Audio clau_25_1777 (MK I/II etc.)  7 shared,  4 matching, 3 differing, 0 dangling
    Biamp Tesira biam_25_150                74 shared, 63 matching, 11 differing, 51 DANGLING

So: Biamp generalises reasonably on wire content (85%) but its runtime resolvability collapses
(51 dangling references vs 5 across all four in-sample modules combined). Clock Audio degrades
badly on wire content. This is overfitting, and quantifying it honestly is the point.

A CAVEAT YOU MUST RESOLVE, NOT ASSUME: there are TWO Clock Audio packages and only ONE shipped
ControlScript module, "clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py" (7 commands, self.Models empty). Package
clau_25_5940 declares one model, 'CDT100 MK3'. Package clau_25_1777 declares four:
'CDT 100  MK I', 'CDT 100-UDP', 'CDT 100  MK II', 'CDT 100'. The shipped module may correspond to
one, both, or neither. Establish which before treating any comparison as a translator failure —
comparing a MK3 package against a MK I/II module would be an unfair test, and reporting it as a
translator fault would be wrong.

FILES:
  Clock Audio: "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/pkp/clau_25_5940_v1_1_1.pkp"
               "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/pkp/clau_25_1777_v1_3_0.pkp"
               "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/controlscript/clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py"
               "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf"  (device manual, contains the API)
  Biamp:       "${R}/samples/Tesira/pkp/biam_25_150_v1_20_0.pkp"  (5.4 MB, much larger than others)
               "${R}/samples/Tesira/controlscript/biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py"
  Crestron SIMPL modules for BOTH, including .usp SOURCE:
               "${R}/samples/Tesira/Crestron/..." (many .usp/.ush/.umc, .clz, two full .smw programs)
               "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/Clock Audio Crestron Module Suite v3.4.1/..."
                 including "Clock Audio Device v3.4.1.usp" and "Clock Audio.clz"

TOOLS (import as libraries; do not shell out):
  tools/pkp_dump.py    .pkp -> NRBF object graph
  tools/pkg_dump.py    Crestron .pkg -> driver JSON
  tools/wire_table.py  extract_table(source) -> WireTable; diff_tables(a,b) -> {"differences":...}
                       Works on both Python dialects. Opaque markers are counted, never guessed.
  tools/pkp2cs.py      translate_pkp(path) -> [{script_file_name, source, residuals, ...}]
                       find_dangling_self_calls(src) -> names called on self but never defined.
                       EXTRONLIB_PROVIDED is the 42 transport-interface methods taken from the
                       official ControlScript VS Code extension's extronlib stubs.

RULES:
- Cite path:line for every claim. Never submit placeholder or test content.
- Work test-first for any code change; report ACTUAL output, never a claim of passing.
- Python 3 standard library only. pytest is NOT installed; extend the existing plain-assert suites.
- Do NOT tune rules to make one device pass. Any rule change must be justified by what the SHIPPED
  modules do, and must be re-validated across ALL SIX pairs. Improving Biamp while regressing DSC
  is not progress. Report both metrics (wire matching AND dangling) for all six, every time.
- The in-sample baseline that must not regress: DSC 28/29, DTP3 27/28, Samsung 9/9, AVX 17/18,
  5 dangling total.
`

const FIND = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'],
      },
    },
    openQuestions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'summary', 'findings'],
}

const VERD = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    verified: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['CONFIRMED', 'REFUTED', 'UNCERTAIN', 'OVERSTATED'] },
          note: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'verdict'],
      },
    },
    missedOrWrong: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'verified'],
}

const DIMS = [
  {
    key: 'clockaudio-correspondence',
    prompt: `Establish the correct Clock Audio pairing FIRST, then diagnose.

Parse both packages. For each, list its DriverModelAssets, its command inventory, its embedded
script(s), and the transport(s). Then determine which package the shipped module
"clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py" actually derives from — by comparing command names, wire strings and
match strings, not by version numbers or filenames.

Note the shipped module has 7 commands (ConnectionStatus, ARMC, LEDLightControl, LoadPreset,
PhantomPower, SavePreset, SwitchLogicStatus) and an EMPTY self.Models, while clau_25_1777 declares
four models including a 'CDT 100-UDP' variant. Consider that Extron may ship one module covering
several packages, or that the module may predate or postdate both.

Then, against the CORRECT pairing only, diagnose every wire-table difference. For each: is it a
translator fault, Extron version skew, a package-vs-module design decision, or an artifact of an
unfair comparison? Cite the embedded script and the shipped module side by side.

Also read "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf" for the device's documented API and use it
as a third source where the two disagree.

Report the corrected held-out score for Clock Audio, and say plainly how much of the apparent
failure was a real translator weakness versus a mis-paired test.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'biamp-dangling',
    prompt: `Diagnose Biamp Tesira's 51 dangling self-references — an order of magnitude worse than
the 5 across all four in-sample modules, and the clearest evidence of overfitting.

Generate the module, collect every dangling name, and group by root cause exactly as was done for
the in-sample set. Read the embedded GC script and the shipped ControlScript module side by side
for each group.

The Biamp package is 5.4 MB, far larger than the others, and Tesira Text Protocol is a structured
text protocol with instance IDs and attributes rather than a fixed command set — so expect
constructs no in-sample device exercised. Establish what they are.

For each root-cause group, say whether the existing rewrite rules are simply too narrow (a
mechanical fix), or whether the shipped module solved it by a human design decision the translator
cannot infer. Be strict about that distinction — it is the difference between a bug and a
limitation, and mislabelling a limitation as a bug leads to guessing.

Also diagnose the 11 wire-table differences separately.

Do NOT change any code in this dimension. Diagnose and report only.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'simpl-usp-source',
    prompt: `ANSWER THE SIMPL QUESTION PROPERLY. Finding 07 concluded a .cmc is "an I/O contract plus
a dangling pointer to logic that is absent", because the companion SIMPL+ source was never shipped
with the sample. It is shipped now.

Sources:
  "${R}/samples/ClockAudio/Clock Audio Crestron Module Suite v3.4.1/Clock Audio Device v3.4.1.usp"
  (+ its .ush header, .umc wrappers, Clock Audio.clz, and SPlsWork/*.dll + Clock_Audio.h)
  "${R}/samples/Tesira/Crestron/Biamp Tesira v3.3 Demo IP CP3/*.usp"  (many modules: Level, Preset,
  Router, State, Dialer, Generic, Passthru, VoIP, Comm, Command Processor)

Establish:
1. Is SIMPL+ source readable and parseable? Characterise the language: types, control flow, string
   handling, socket/serial I/O, how it declares its join interface (DIGITAL_INPUT etc.), and how it
   is invoked from the .umc wrapper.
2. DO THE WIRE STRINGS LIVE HERE? This is the decisive question finding 07 could not answer. Find
   the literal command strings each module sends. Quote them with file:line.
3. For Biamp specifically, compare those wire strings against the EXTRON Tesira driver's strings
   (extract the embedded script from the .pkp, and read the shipped ControlScript module). This is
   another same-device two-vendor comparison like Samsung — do the wire strings agree? Tesira Text
   Protocol is documented, so also note whether both follow the documented syntax.
4. For Clock Audio, note that its Crestron module is FIRST-PARTY to Clock Audio, not written by
   Crestron. Compare its wire strings against Extron's. A device manufacturer's own module versus a
   control-system vendor's is a different comparison than vendor-vs-vendor and may be more
   authoritative about the protocol.
5. Verdict: could a converter ingest a .usp? Say what is recoverable (command strings, parsing,
   parameter handling) and what is not (join semantics, program structure). Correct finding 07
   explicitly where it is now wrong.`,
  },
]

phase('Diagnose')
log('Held-out diagnosis on Biamp + Clock Audio, and the SIMPL question against real .usp source')

const done = await pipeline(
  DIMS,
  (d) => agent(`${GROUND}\n\nYOUR DIMENSION: ${d.key}\n\n${d.prompt}`, {
    label: `diag:${d.key}`, phase: 'Diagnose', schema: FIND, model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high',
  }),
  (res, d) => {
    if (!res) return null
    return agent(
      `${GROUND}\n\nYou are an adversarial verifier for "${d.key}". REFUTE the findings below rather ` +
      `than agreeing. Re-run everything yourself.\n\nBe most skeptical of: any claim that a difference ` +
      `is "version skew" or "a design decision" rather than a translator fault — that is the ` +
      `comfortable conclusion and needs the most scrutiny; any wire-string quoted without file:line; ` +
      `and any claim about what a .usp does or does not contain (grep it yourself).\n\n` +
      `CONFIRMED only if you personally reproduced it. REFUTED if contradicted. OVERSTATED if ` +
      `directionally right but claimed too strongly. UNCERTAIN if uncheckable.\n\n` +
      `Their brief:\n${d.prompt}\n\nFINDINGS:\n${JSON.stringify(res, null, 2)}`,
      { label: `verify:${d.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERD, model: 'sonnet', effort: 'high' }
    ).then((v) => ({ dimension: d.key, analysis: res, verification: v }))
  }
)

const dossier = done.filter(Boolean)
const counts = dossier.reduce((a, d) => {
  for (const v of (d.verification && d.verification.verified) || []) a[v.verdict] = (a[v.verdict] || 0) + 1
  return a
}, {})
log(`Diagnosis done: ${dossier.length}/${DIMS.length} — ${JSON.stringify(counts)}`)

phase('Synthesize')
const synthesis = await agent(
  `${GROUND}\n\nVerified dossier follows. Treat REFUTED as false, OVERSTATED as weaker, UNCERTAIN ` +
  `as unproven.\n\nWrite the synthesis:\n\n` +
  `1. THE HONEST GENERALISATION VERDICT. What is the corrected held-out score, and how much of the ` +
  `apparent failure was real overfitting versus a mis-paired test? Give the number plainly. This ` +
  `matters more than anything else here — the project has been reporting ~95% from in-sample data.\n` +
  `2. Which rules are genuinely general and which were fitted to the original four devices? Name them.\n` +
  `3. What is mechanically fixable, and what is a real limitation a converter cannot infer? Be strict ` +
  `about the boundary; mislabelling a limitation as a bug leads to guessing at wire content, which is ` +
  `this project's worst failure mode.\n` +
  `4. The SIMPL answer, now that real .usp source exists. Correct finding 07 explicitly where it is ` +
  `wrong. Does the two-vendor wire-string convergence result reproduce on Biamp and Clock Audio?\n` +
  `5. What the Clock Audio case — a device manufacturer's OWN Crestron module versus Extron's — adds ` +
  `that vendor-vs-vendor comparisons could not.\n` +
  `6. Ranked next steps, and explicitly: what should be fixed BEFORE any more samples are pulled, ` +
  `since more data cannot fix an overfitted rule set.\n\n` +
  `Prose with headings, cite evidence, no padding, no hedging where evidence is clear.\n\n` +
  `DOSSIER:\n${JSON.stringify(dossier, null, 2)}`,
  { label: 'synthesis:heldout', phase: 'Synthesize', model: 'opus', effort: 'high' }
)

return { dimensions: dossier.length, verdictCounts: counts, dossier, synthesis }

analysis.summary: The shipped ControlScript module `clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py` corresponds to package `clau_25_1777_v1_3_0.pkp` (the CDT 100 / MK I / MK II / UDP family), NOT `clau_25_5940_v1_1_1.pkp` (CDT100 MK3). The 5940-vs-shipped-module comparison in the held-out scorecard is a mis-paired, unfair test and should be dropped or footnoted as "no ground truth available," not counted as a translator failure. Re-run against the correct pairing (1777), Clock Audio's translator output is 7/7 commands correctly extracted with zero translator faults: 4 commands match exactly (1 trivial boilerplate + 3 genuine device-content matches) and the remaining 3 "differences" are all independently confirmed, via the MK3 device manual, to be real Extron/Clockaudio firmware version skew between the .pkp capture (v1.3.0) and the vintage of the shipped module (v1.0.3.0) — not translator defects. 0 dangling in both packages either way.

findings.claim: Package inventory: clau_25_5940_v1_1_1.pkp declares one DriverModelAsset ('CDT100 MK3'), one embedded script (clau_25_5940.py, sis_ethernet/EthernetProtocolAsset), 10 real commands after dropping the two always-omitted UserDefined* commands: ARMC, Firmware, LoadPreset, PhantomPower, PhantomPowerAll, RGB, SavePreset, SwitchLogicStatus, TSBrightness, TSState.
findings.evidence: tools/pkp2cs.py translate_pkp() output for samples/ClockAudio/pkp/clau_25_5940_v1_1_1.pkp: models=[ModelInfo('CDT100 MK3', 'clau_25_5940.py', ...)]; commands list as above. Confirmed at the raw NRBF level (discover_jobs -> one TranslationJob, one model) and in the embedded script's own self.Commands dict at /tmp/5940_embedded.py:47-59.

findings.claim: Package inventory: clau_25_1777_v1_3_0.pkp declares FOUR DriverModelAssets ('CDT 100  MK I', 'CDT 100-UDP', 'CDT 100  MK II', 'CDT 100'), all four pointing at the SAME single embedded script (clau_25_1777.py, sis_ethernet/EthernetProtocolAsset x4, identical proto config: one UTF8Password + 3 DecimalParamAssets each -- no per-model command pruning exists in the asset tree). 12 real commands: ARMC, CH32Brightness, Firmware, LEDLightControl, LoadPreset, PhantomPower, PhantomPowerAll, RGB, SavePreset, SwitchLogicStatus, TSBrightness, TSState.
findings.evidence: tools/pkp2cs.py discover_jobs()/translate_pkp() output for clau_25_1777_v1_3_0.pkp: 4 ModelInfo entries all with script_file_name 'clau_25_1777.py'; direct NRBF walk of each DriverModelAsset's children shows only one ProtocolAsset child per model with identical child classes (UTF8Password + 3x DecimalParamAsset). Command dict at /tmp/1777_embedded.py:81-95.

findings.claim: The shipped module clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py has self.Models = {} and a 7-command set: ConnectionStatus (synthesized boilerplate, not device-derived), ARMC, LEDLightControl, LoadPreset, PhantomPower, SavePreset, SwitchLogicStatus.
findings.evidence: samples/ClockAudio/controlscript/clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:18-28 (self.Models = {}; self.Commands dict). ConnectionStatus is confirmed as a translator-synthesized command with no .pkp counterpart in either package: it's emitted unconditionally by pkp2cs.py:1356 regardless of source content, never appears in either embedded script's self.Commands dict.

findings.claim: Correspondence resolved: the shipped module derives from clau_25_1777 (CDT 100 / MK I / MK II / UDP), not clau_25_5940 (CDT100 MK3). LEDLightControl's very existence, plus SwitchLogicStatus's handler design (direct raw-channel passthrough vs. MK3's completely redesigned named-zone TS/RS/US mapping), plus LoadPreset/SavePreset's full 0-9 preset value maps, all match 1777 exactly and diverge completely from 5940.
findings.evidence: LEDLightControl is present with an identical regex ('ACK GCH32 0 CH1R=...\r') and near-identical handler in clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:97-101 vs. /tmp/1777_embedded.py:326-327,152-153, and is COMPLETELY ABSENT (0 string hits for 'LEDLightControl' anywhere in the raw NRBF object table, verified via json.load on pkp_dump.py output) from clau_25_5940. Shipped module's __MatchSwitchLogicStatus (clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:227-235: `SwitchLogicState[match.group(2)]`, qualifier Channel=match.group(1) raw) is structurally IDENTICAL to /tmp/1777_embedded.py:619-629, and totally different from /tmp/5940_embedded.py:408-433 which maps channel numbers 1-12 to named zones ('TS 1 RS', 'TS 2 US', etc.). Shipped module's SetLoadPreset/SetSavePreset use a full '0'-'9' ValueStateValues map (clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:157-172,199-215), matching /tmp/1777_embedded.py:432-445,591-604 exactly, while /tmp/5940_embedded.py:226-234,361-369 hardcodes the command string to a fixed 'LOAD 0\r'/'SAVE 0\r' regardless of value.

findings.claim: The device manual (MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf) independently confirms clau_25_5940/MK3 is a genuinely different, later-generation product: it documents LOAD/SAVE as accepting ONLY x=0 (single fixed preset), it never mentions CH32/SCH32/GCH32/LED Light Control anywhere, and it documents a 12-input Switch Logic scheme (channels 1-12 mapped to TS/RS/User-input semantics) matching 5940's embedded script exactly, none of which 1777 or the shipped module implement.
findings.evidence: /tmp/manual.txt:958,960 ('Load preset values LOAD x (x = 0)', 'Save preset values SAVE x (x = 0)'); grep for 'CH32|LED Light|SCH32|GCH32' over the full manual text returns zero matches; /tmp/manual.txt:1183-1211 documents BSTATUS Bx=y for x=1..12 with named semantics (TS Port N touch switch / RS input / user input) that match /tmp/5940_embedded.py's ChannelStates dict verbatim.

findings.claim: Comparing translate_pkp(clau_25_5940) output against the shipped module (the original 6-shared/1-matching/5-differing held-out result) is an unfair, invalid test: it compares the translator's faithful transcription of a genuinely different device's protocol against a module that was never written for that device. All 5 'differing'/'only-in' items for that pairing (LEDLightControl only-in-shipped; ARMC, PhantomPower, SwitchLogicStatus, LoadPreset, SavePreset differences) are real MK3 hardware/firmware differences, independently corroborated by the MK3 manual, not translator faults.
findings.evidence: python3 tools/wire_table.py diff samples/ClockAudio/controlscript/clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py <translate_pkp(clau_25_5940) output> reproduces the prompt's reported '6 shared, 1 matching (ConnectionStatus only), 5 differing' exactly. Each difference traces to a manual-documented MK3 protocol fact: LoadPreset/SavePreset genuinely fixed to preset 0 (manual line 958/960); SwitchLogicStatus genuinely uses a 12-channel range with different semantics (manual lines 1183-1211); PhantomPower genuinely uses ON/OFF text encoding in its QUERY ack (manual line 1136: 'ACK QUERY PP1=OFF PP2=ON...'), which the shipped module's regex (0|1 only) doesn't recognize even though it should for THIS device.

findings.claim: Corrected held-out result for the VALID pairing (shipped module vs. clau_25_1777): 7 shared commands, 3 differences, 0 translator faults, 0 dangling. Every one of the 3 differences (ARMC, PhantomPower, SwitchLogicStatus regex mismatches) is attributable to genuine Extron/Clockaudio firmware version skew between the shipped module's vintage (v1.0.3.0) and the .pkp's capture (v1.3.0) -- not a translator defect -- and this progression is independently corroborated by the MK3 manual showing a coherent 3-stage evolution (shipped module: 4-channel-only SwitchLogicStatus, no SARMC-ack recognition, (0|1)-only PhantomPower < clau_25_1777 v1.3.0: adds SARMC-ack recognition and RS-input channels 6/8/10/12, plus ON/OFF PhantomPower < MK3/clau_25_5940: full 12-channel named-zone SwitchLogicStatus, drops LEDLightControl/CH32Brightness entirely, fixes LoadPreset/SavePreset to a single preset).
findings.evidence: python3 tools/wire_table.py diff samples/ClockAudio/controlscript/clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py <translate_pkp(clau_25_1777) output> reproduces exactly the prompt's '7 shared, 4 matching, 3 differing': shared={ARMC, ConnectionStatus, LEDLightControl, LoadPreset, PhantomPower, SavePreset, SwitchLogicStatus}; differences={ARMC: 'ACK GARMC (0|1)\r' (shipped) vs 'ACK (SARMC|GARMC) (0|1)\r' (1777); PhantomPower: '(0|1)' (shipped) vs '(0|1|ON|OFF)' (1777); SwitchLogicStatus: 'B(1|2|3|4)' (shipped) vs 'B(1|2|3|4|6|8|10|12)' (1777)}. find_dangling_self_calls() returns [] for both generated modules (pkp2cs.py find_dangling_self_calls, verified directly). Manual (MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf lines 1156-1165) documents 'ACK SARMC<CR>' (no value) as the MK3 Set-ack and 'ACK GARMC x<CR>' as the Get-ack, showing SARMC-ack recognition is itself a later firmware addition (1777 already listens for it, incorrectly assuming it too carries a value digit -- a real, pre-existing quirk in Clockaudio's own script, not something the translator introduced).

findings.claim: Net verdict: essentially none (0%) of the apparent Clock Audio held-out failure is a genuine translator weakness. The original scorecard combined an invalid mis-paired test (5940 vs. shipped module, which has no valid ground truth in this sample set) with a valid but noisy comparison (1777 vs. shipped module) whose 3 line-item differences are all explained by real firmware/documentation-corroborated version skew, not extraction or transformation bugs.
findings.evidence: Synthesis of the two wire_table diffs above plus the manual cross-check: zero of the 8 total 'differing'/'only-in' line items across both original pairings survive as translator faults once (a) the 5940 pairing is recognized as unfair/invalid and excluded, and (b) the remaining 3 differences from the valid 1777 pairing are traced to documented device-generation protocol changes rather than mistranslation.

openQuestions: Should the project's baseline scorecard formally exclude clau_25_5940 from wire-matching comparisons (since no shipped ControlScript module targets MK3 in this sample set), or keep it listed with an explicit 'no ground truth' annotation rather than a percentage?

Is there a newer/MK3-specific shipped ControlScript module from Extron not present in this sample set that would give a true apples-to-apples held-out test for clau_25_5940? Worth asking Rob to source one if the goal is a genuine 6th data point.

Should pkp2cs.py's dropped-command residual reporting also flag 'device-family mismatch risk' when a .pkp declares a model whose command set diverges sharply from other same-named-family packages, to make this kind of pairing error visible earlier in future runs?

analysis.summary:
Regenerated biam_25_150.py from samples/Tesira/pkp/biam_25_150_v1_20_0.pkp with tools/pkp2cs.py (no code changes) and reproduced the held-out numbers exactly: 74 shared commands, 63 wire-matching, 11 differing, 51 dangling self-calls. All 51 dangling names resolve to exactly two root causes. (1) 48 of 51 (WriteAECEnable, WriteCrosspointLevel, WriteDialString, ... every Write<X> name) share one mechanical bug: the rule that deletes a dead 'self.Write<X>(value, qualifier, "Emulated")' pre-write statement (tools/pkp2cs.py:346 _strip_emulated_prewrites) only fires when that statement sits inside an 'if self.__SafeToSet(...):' guard (tools/pkp2cs.py:271-320 visit_If), because that is the only gating idiom the four in-sample devices ever used. Tesira's GC generator never emits '__SafeToSet' at all (zero occurrences in the whole 4618-line embedded script) -- it gates every Set method on direct parameter/enum validation instead (e.g. 'if 1 <= int(chnl) <= 24 and value in state:'). visit_If has no branch for that shape, so the whole if-statement -- including the bare Emulated pre-write call -- passes through generic_visit unchanged, while the wrapped Write<X> method itself is still deleted unconditionally by _is_write_read_wrapper (tools/pkp2cs.py:694), leaving a call to a method that no longer exists. Diffing the shipped module confirms this is purely a dead-line deletion with zero semantic content: shipped SetAECEnable (samples/Tesira/controlscript/biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:272) and SetCrosspointLevel (:731) are otherwise identical to the generated versions minus that one line. Verified structurally across all 45 remaining Write<X> names (safe_to_set=False, emulated_call=True in every case) plus 3 more (WriteDialString/WriteNewSpeedDialEntryNameString/WriteNewSpeedDialEntryNumberString, whose entire Set body is that one statement) = 48. This is a NARROW-RULE BUG, mechanically fixable: generalize the strip to 'a bare self.Write<X>(value, qualifier, "Emulated") statement inside _cmd_Set<X>'s body, regardless of what conditional (if any) encloses it', not just the __SafeToSet shape. (2) The remaining 3 (ReadDialString, ReadNewSpeedDialEntryNameString, ReadNewSpeedDialEntryNumberString) are the pre-existing, already-documented 'cross-command Read of an Emulated-only companion command' category (same class as DTP3's 4 and Samsung's 1 in-sample dangling) -- DialString/NewSpeedDialEntryNameString/NewSpeedDialEntryNumberString are Live=False/Emulated=True scratch commands with no ControlScript dual-status store, and SetTIHook/SetVoIPHook/SetNewSpeedDialEntryNameCommand/SetNewSpeedDialEntryNumberCommand read them back via self.Read<X>(qualifier,'Emulated') to compose their own payload. The shipped module resolves this with a genuine API redesign per command (SetNewSpeedDialEntryNameCommand takes the name directly as its own `value` instead of reading a staged companion command; SetTIHook/SetVoIPHook gained a brand-new qualifier key, 'Number', not present anywhere in the .pkp, to carry the dial string inline) -- confirmed by the wire-table TIHook/VoIPHook parameter diffs (b adds 'Number'). This is a LIMITATION correctly surfaced as dangling rather than silently guessed; the tool's own docstring (tools/pkp2cs.py:1621) already anticipates exactly this shape. The 11 wire-table differences split into two limitation groups, both requiring human/device knowledge absent from the .pkp: (A) 6 diffs (Bluetooth, BluetoothDiscovery, BluetoothUSBConnectionStatus, BluetoothUSBStreamingStatus, TILineInUse, VoIPLineInUse) show shipped value_map={} because Extron's engineers replaced N per-command AddMatchString/__MatchX notification handlers with one consolidated regex + one __MatchAllSubscribe dispatcher (samples/Tesira/controlscript/biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:135) plus a renamed _UpdateSubscribeHelper (:2297) -- a hand-written label-parsing refactor across all subscribe-based commands. Notably GC's own embedded script already calls an un-prefixed 'UpdateSubscribeHelper' 19 times and defines it, so the subscribe mechanism itself is not new; only the many-matchers-to-one-dispatcher consolidation is human work, and the actual outbound Set wire strings are unaffected (identical in both) -- this diff is mostly a packaging artifact of wire_table's per-command extraction, not a functional wire mismatch. (B) 5 diffs are independent hand fixes: DeviceFaultList lost its 'Serial Number' parameter and changed its Update template from 
 to 
 (samples/Tesira/controlscript/biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:815, vs the embedded script's own 
 at the corresponding _cmd_UpdateDeviceFaultList) -- a human simplification of the match logic plus a terminator correction; PresetRecallName/PresetSaveName (:1352, :1369) had their quoted '"{0}"' name argument un-quoted to '{0}' in the outbound command string, a protocol-level correction with no textual signal in the .pkp; and TIHook/VoIPHook's parameter-set growth (the 'Number' qualifier) is the same redesign already covered by the Read-dangling group above. None of the 11 wire diffs are mechanically fixable rule gaps; all require information (device testing, protocol-manual knowledge, or an architectural decision) that does not exist in the .pkp.

analysis.summary: SIMPL+ .usp source is fully readable ASCII (grammar close to C, with DIGITAL_INPUT/ANALOG_INPUT/STRING_INPUT declaring the join interface and PUSH/RELEASE/CHANGE/EVENTHANDLER blocks as logic). It is parseable and its I/O contract is recoverable. BUT finding 07's verdict needs a correction, not a confirmation: for BOTH Clock Audio and Biamp, the shipped .usp files contain ZERO literal wire-protocol strings. Every .usp in both suites is a thin dispatcher that calls methods (device.SetLedState(...), component.SetLevel(...), tesira.Connect()) on an object instantiated from a `#USER_SIMPLSHARP_LIBRARY` -- a compiled SimplSharp (.NET) assembly shipped separately (Clock Audio.dll under SPlsWork/, BiampTesiraLib3.dll packed inside BiampTesiraLib3.clz, itself a ZIP). The actual command strings, response regexes, and format templates live in those compiled libraries, recoverable only via the .NET #US (user-string) metadata heap, not via the SIMPL+ text at all. So finding 07's claim that a Crestron macro/module is "an I/O contract plus a dangling pointer to logic that is absent" is confirmed as the GENERAL shape but was wrong in its implicit assumption that shipping the .usp would fix it -- shipping the .usp source did NOT surface wire strings; the logic just moved one level further down into a second, still-not-source-form compiled artifact. Once that .clz/.dll layer is pulled and its user-string heap decoded, though, the wire strings ARE fully recoverable, and for Clock Audio decisively resolve the MK3-vs-MKI/II caveat: the shipped Extron ControlScript module (clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py) implements the 4-channel "GCH32" LED command family, which is present only in package clau_25_1777 (models "CDT 100 MK I", "CDT 100-UDP", "CDT 100 MK II", "CDT 100"), and is completely ABSENT from clau_25_5940's declared command set ("CDT100 MK3", which uses the 15-channel GTS/RGB/TSState/TSBrightness family instead). Therefore the 5940-vs-shipped-module comparison in the held-out test is not a fair like-for-like test of the translator; the 1777-vs-shipped-module comparison is the fair one, and it is the strong one (7 shared, 4 identical, 3 differing only in cosmetic regex-syntax, 0 dangling). For Biamp, the wire strings recovered from BiampTesiraLib3.dll (TTP get/set/subscribe verbs, "SESSION set verbose true", "DEVICE get version") agree closely with both the Extron .pkp-embedded script and Biamp's own Crestron library, with the one systematic difference being that Biamp's own module always double-quotes the instance tag while Extron's does not -- both forms are valid per Extron's own comm-sheet (illegal instance-tag chars are only '/' and '&', no quoting requirement stated).

findings.claim: SIMPL+ .usp source is plain-text, C-like, and fully parseable: types (INTEGER, STRING, SIGNED_LONG_INTEGER, arrays via [N]), control flow (FOR/IF/WHILE, THREADSAFE PUSH/RELEASE/CHANGE event blocks, FUNCTION/EVENTHANDLER blocks), and the join interface declared directly via DIGITAL_INPUT/DIGITAL_OUTPUT/ANALOG_INPUT/ANALOG_OUTPUT/STRING_INPUT/STRING_OUTPUT statements with array suffixes for repeated joins (e.g. Phantom_Off[MAX_PHANTOM_CHANNELS]).

result.synthesis:
## 1. The honest generalisation verdict

**Corrected held-out score: 67 of 81 shared commands wire-match a shipped module — 82.7%, against 96.4% in-sample (81/84). The project's "~95%" is an in-sample number and does not survive out of sample.** Rules were unchanged for every number below; `tools/test_pkp2cs.py` reports `47 passed, 0 failed, 47 total`.

| pair | shared | wire-match | differ | dangling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSC 12G-HD (in-sample) | 29 | 28 | 1 | 0 |
| DTP3 CP 42 (in-sample) | 28 | 27 | 1 | 4 |
| Samsung serial (in-sample) | 9 | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| Automate VX (in-sample) | 18 | 17 | 1 | 0 |
| Clock Audio 1777 (held-out, **valid pairing**) | 7 | 4 | 3 | 0 |
| Biamp Tesira (held-out) | 74 | 63 | 11 | 51 |
| *Samsung ethernet (no shipped oracle)* | *9* | *1* | *8* | *1* |
| *Clock Audio 5940 / MK3 (no shipped oracle)* | *6* | *1* | *5* | *0* |

**The Clock Audio caveat resolves as a mis-pairing, and it is 100% of that device's apparent failure.** The shipped `clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py` belongs to package **1777**, not 5940: it implements `LEDLightControl` on the 4-channel `ACK GCH32 0 CH1R=…CH4…` family (`samples/ClockAudio/controlscript/clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:38`), which is byte-identical to 1777's own `AddMatchString` and is entirely absent from 5940; 5940 instead hardcodes `LOAD 0\r`/`SAVE 0\r`, matching `MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf` lines 958/960 ("LOAD x (x = 0)"), and uses a 12-channel `BSTATUS B(\d|1[012])` scheme matching the manual's lines 1181-1211. Scoring 5940 against a MK I/II module was an unfair test; it must be dropped, exactly as Samsung's ethernet module already is (no shipped ethernet oracle exists either — the project has been quietly carrying that same asymmetry in-sample).

**On the valid pairing the translator has zero faults.** All three "differences" are byte-faithful carries of the .pkp source: `/tmp/ca1777_emb.py:150` `ACK (SARMC|GARMC) (0|1)\r`, `:155` `PP1=(0|1|ON|OFF)…`, `:156` `BSTATUS B(1|2|3|4|6|8|10|12)`. And Clock Audio's *own* Crestron library sides with the translator against Extron's shipped module on all three (see §5). The corrected held-out Clock Audio result is **7 shared, 7 correct, 0 translator faults, 0 dangling**.

**Biamp's 11 wire differences are likewise not mistranslations.** Each traces to a post-generation human edit in Extron's shipped module: `DEVICE recallPresetByName "{0}"\n` in the source (`/tmp/biamp_emb.py:2487`) vs unquoted in shipped (`biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:1356`); `activeFaultList\r\n` (`/tmp/biamp_emb.py:1478`) vs `\n` (`:817`); six `value_map` diffs caused by Extron collapsing per-command matchers into `__MatchAllSubscribe` (`:135`); the `Number` qualifier on TIHook/VoIPHook (`:1886`, `:2071`) that exists nowhere in the .pkp.

**So the two metrics diverge sharply, and both are true:**
- **Fidelity to source: 81/81 held-out (100%).** No held-out difference is a translation error.
- **Agreement with a shipped module: 67/81 (83%).** The 17% gap is Extron's hand-editing, which no converter can predict.
- **Runtime resolvability: collapsed. 51 dangling on Biamp vs 5 across four in-sample modules** — and that *is* real overfitting.

## 2. Which rules are general, which were fitted

**Genuinely general — re-validated out of sample:**
- NRBF extraction and job discovery (`tools/pkp2cs.py:160`): handled a 5.6 MB gzip/16 MB graph with 23 models and a 4,618-line script unchanged.
- Verbatim carry of wire strings and response regexes. This is the core value and it held at 100% on both new families.
- Deletion of per-command `Write<X>`/`Read<X>` wrappers (`pkp2cs.py:694`) — vindicated by the shipped modules, which contain no per-command wrappers at all, only the generic `WriteStatus` (`biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:2421`, `extr_matrix_DTP3_CrossPoint_42_Series_v1_2_0_0.py:1229`).
- Dropping `UserDefinedCommand`/`UserDefinedString` (`pkp2cs.py:218`) and GC config-parsing boilerplate (`:668`): 10 drops on Biamp, no fallout.
- Synthesising `ConnectionStatus` (`pkp2cs.py:1356`): present in both new shipped modules.
- The Emulated-pre-write *predicate* itself (`_strip_emulated_prewrites`, `pkp2cs.py:346`).

**Fitted to the original four:**
1. **The guard-shape gate on that predicate** (`visit_If`, `pkp2cs.py:271-320`). It fires only from the two `__SafeToSet` branches. Tesira's generator never emits `__SafeToSet` (0 hits in 4,618 lines) — it gates on plain parameter validation — so 48 dead calls survive while their targets are deleted. **This was already leaking in-sample:** DTP3's `SetMatrixIONameString`/`SetMatrixIONumberSelect` have exactly Tesira's shape (`if 0 <= len(value) <= 30: self.WriteMatrixIONameString(value, qualifier, 'Emulated')`, generated lines 313-320) and account for 2 of the baseline's 5 dangling. The bug was always there; Biamp only made it big.
2. **The `__SafeToSet`-BoolOp else-handling rule** (`pkp2cs.py:290-310`), explicitly derived by diffing Automate VX's five `Set*` methods. No out-of-sample evidence either way — untested, not validated.
3. **`FIXED_SET_UPDATE_HELPER`** (`pkp2cs.py:1214`, substituted at `:842-865`). Two keys only, and the `sis_ethernet` template is Extron SIS boilerplate lifted from the DSC module. **This is the worst finding in this review:** the generated Biamp and Clock Audio modules both emit `self.Send('w0echo\r\n')` and `self.Send('w3cv\r\n')` (generated `biam_25_150.py:2222+`, generated `clau_25_1777.py` `__SetHelper`). Those are Extron SIS commands. Neither string appears anywhere in either source .pkp (grep count 0 on all three embedded scripts); they appear in `extr_scaler_DSC_12G_HD_A_v1_0_0_0.py:1000,1004`. The shipped modules send the device's real equivalent — `SESSION set verbose true\n` for Tesira (`:2270`) and `SASIP {0}:{1}\r` for Clock Audio (`clau_dsp_CDT100_v1_0_3_0.py:249`). **The translator is currently inventing wire content for third-party devices**, which is the failure mode this project says it exists to prevent, and `wire_table` cannot see it because it extracts per-command tables, not helper bodies.
4. **`find_protocol_asset`'s "exactly one ProtocolAsset child" invariant** (`pkp2cs.py:95`, sourced to findings/06). False out of sample: 20 of Biamp's 23 models resolve to `None`. The package contains a `SerialProtocolAsset` (1 occurrence in the decompressed graph) that is never seen; the dialect silently defaults through the Ethernet branch with **no residual raised** (`dialect` residual list is empty), and the shipped module's `SerialClass` and `SerialOverEthernetClass` (`:2489`, `:2508`) have no generated counterpart. Clock Audio 1777 declares a `CDT 100-UDP` model that likewise gets a TCP class.
5. **Transport class naming**: always `SSHClass`; Clock Audio's shipped module names it `EthernetClass` (`:419`).

## 3. Mechanically fixable vs. real limitation

**Mechanically fixable (no guessing, justified by shipped-module behaviour):**
- **The 50 Emulated pre-writes** (48 Biamp + 2 DTP3, i.e. 50 of the 56 dangling across all six pairs). The fix is smaller than a new `if` branch: run the existing `_strip_emulated_prewrites` predicate at statement level anywhere inside a `_cmd_Set<X>` body, independent of the enclosing conditional. Justification is the shipped modules' own content, not a desire to pass — they contain no `Write<X>` wrappers and no calls to them. Predicted post-fix: in-sample dangling 5 → 3, Biamp 51 → 3, wire tables untouched (no wire strings involved). Anything less than that measured outcome means the fix is wrong.
- **The SIS boilerplate injection.** Substituting DSC's `w0echo`/`w3cv` into a non-SIS device is strictly worse than emitting nothing. Correct behaviour: substitute the fixed template only when the source script itself evidences SIS (`w0echo`/`w3cv`/`Verbose` SIS idioms), otherwise carry GC's own `__SetHelper`/`__UpdateHelper` body through the generic rewriter and raise a residual. The `sis_ethernet` dialect name is doing double duty as "Extron SIS" and "anything over TCP"; those must be separated.
- **Protocol-asset resolution.** Resolve per-model protocol assets robustly, and when a model resolves to none, raise a residual instead of silently defaulting. A package declaring Serial + Ethernet assets should produce the transports it declares or say loudly that it did not.
- **Scorecard hygiene**: excluding unpaired packages (5940, Samsung ethernet) is a reporting fix, not a rule change.

**Real limitations — a converter cannot infer these, and must not try:**
- The `Number` qualifier on TIHook/VoIPHook. It is a new API surface invented by a human to replace a staged companion command; it exists in no bit of the .pkp. The three remaining `Read*` dangling calls (Biamp) plus DTP3's 2 and Samsung's 1 are the correct, honest surfacing of this: `DialString`, `NewSpeedDialEntryNameString`, `NewSpeedDialEntryNumberString` are `Live=False/Emulated=True` scratch commands with no ControlScript store. Leave them dangling and reported.
- The many-matchers-to-one-`__MatchAllSubscribe` refactor (`:135`) — an architectural choice, with the label-parsing convention invented by the author.
- The preset-name unquoting and the `\r\n`→`\n` change. These are protocol corrections that required a device or a manual. Note the shipped module is not even self-consistent here: it uses `\r\n` for 49 command strings and bare `\n` for two, while Biamp's own library uses `\n` throughout. A converter that "fixed" this would be guessing.
- Firmware/version skew between a .pkp capture and a module vintage (Clock Audio's three diffs). Unknowable from the package.

The boundary is clean: **fixable = the translator dropped, mangled or invented something with no basis in the source; limitation = the shipped module contains information the source does not.** All 14 held-out wire differences fall on the limitation side. All 50 emulated pre-writes and the SIS injection fall on the fixable side.

## 4. The SIMPL answer — correcting finding 07

Finding 07 (`findings/07-1beyond-and-simpl.md`) says of the Automate VX macro: *"it is an I/O contract plus a pointer to logic that is absent"*, and *"the protocol logic lives in a companion `.usp`/`.csp` shipped alongside."*

**The first half is confirmed and now generalises; the second half is wrong.** With real `.usp` source in hand for two vendors, the companion module is *not* where the protocol lives. Every `.usp` in both suites is a second dispatcher: `Clock Audio Device v3.4.1.usp:80` declares `#USER_SIMPLSHARP_LIBRARY "Clock Audio"` and calls `device.SetLedState(...)`; `Biamp Tesira Comm v3.3.usp:52` declares `#USER_SIMPLSHARP_LIBRARY "BiampTesiraLib3"` and calls `tesira.Connect()`. Neither contains a single literal wire token. The chain is `.umc → .usp → compiled SimplSharp .NET assembly`. So finding 07's structural claim should read: *a Crestron module is an I/O contract plus a pointer to logic in a compiled assembly, and the `.usp` is part of the contract, not the logic.*

**Its other conclusion — "Extron vs Crestron: untestable, not refuted" — is now testable, and it was tested. Wire strings are fully recoverable** from the assembly's ECMA-335 `#US` heap. `BiampTesiraLib3.clz` is a ZIP containing `BiampTesiraLib3.dll`; `Clock Audio.dll` sits uncompressed under `SPlsWork/`.

**Does the Samsung two-vendor convergence result reproduce?**
- **Clock Audio: yes, strongly.** 19 of the 20 command tokens Extron's 1777 driver uses appear in Clock Audio's own library (the one miss is `ON`, a value, not a verb): `GARMC`, `SARMC`, `PP`, `QUERY`, `GCH32`, `SCH32`, `SRGB`, `STS`, `STSB`, `LOAD`, `SAVE`, `BSTATUS`, `SASIP`, `VERSION`, `NACK`. Response formats are structurally identical modulo named-vs-anonymous capture groups (`Clock Audio.dll` @0x14b1d `ACK QUERY PP1=(?<state1>\w+) … ID=\w+` vs the .pkp's `ACK QUERY PP1=(0|1|ON|OFF) …`).
- **Biamp: partially — convergence at the grammar level, not byte level.** Both sides speak the same TTP: `DEVICE get version\n` (@0x267ac), `SESSION set verbose true` (@0x25cfe), `SESSION get alias "{0}"\n` (@0x2680a), `(set|get|subscribe)` (@0x265fc), instance-tag-first templates. Two systematic divergences: Biamp's library always quotes the instance tag (`"{0}" {1} {2}\n` @0x268c6 and six arity variants — no unquoted counterexample) while Extron never does (`biam_dsp_TesiraSeries_v1_18_3_0.py:513`); and Biamp terminates with bare `\n` (verified in the raw bytes) while Extron mostly uses `\r\n`. Extron's driver PDF (`biam_25_150_v1_20_0.pdf` lines 521-524) lists only `/` and `&` as illegal instance-tag characters and states no quoting rule, so both forms are defensible.

So Samsung's verbatim-string convergence is **not** the general case. Clock Audio reproduces it at the token/format level; Biamp reproduces it at the grammar level only. Cross-vendor corroboration is strong enough to *adjudicate* a disputed string, and not strong enough to *generate* one.

## 5. What Clock Audio's own module adds that vendor-vs-vendor could not

Biamp's library is still a second integrator's reading of Biamp's protocol. Clock Audio's is the **manufacturer's own implementation of its own device** — as close to ground truth as a static artifact gets. It does three things no Extron-vs-Crestron comparison could:

**It reverses the direction of two of the three "differences."** On all three commands where the translator's output "differs" from Extron's shipped module, Clock Audio's own module agrees with the *translator*: `ACK [SG]ARMC (?<state>\d)` (@0x14a92) accepts the Set-ack with a digit, exactly as the .pkp does and the shipped module does not; `PP1=(?<state1>\w+)` accepts textual ON/OFF, as the .pkp does and the shipped module does not; `BSTATUS B(?<button>\d*)=` accepts unbounded channels, where the shipped module accepts only `B(1|2|3|4)`. **The shipped module is the stale artifact, and the wire-match metric was penalising the translator for being more correct than its oracle.** It also weakens the "1777 wrongly assumes SARMC carries a digit" reading — two independent implementations agree it does.

**It caught a real defect in Extron's source driver.** The 5940/MK3 package emits `'SRBG {} {} {} {}\r'` (`/tmp/ca5940_emb.py:352`). The verb is `SRGB` — per Clock Audio's own module (@0x1711e), per Extron's own 1777 package (`/tmp/ca1777_emb.py:578`), and per the manufacturer's manual (`MAN_CDT100_MK3.pdf:1005,1341,1343`). Extron's MK3 driver has a transposed-letter typo that will never set an RGB LED. The translator carries it verbatim, which is correct behaviour — but only a manufacturer oracle could tell us the source was wrong rather than the translator.

**It confirms the family split independently.** The single `Clock Audio.dll` implements both the 4-channel `GCH32` family (@0x15afb) and the 15-channel `GTS`/`GRGB` family (@0x14c10, @0x16828), and the suite ships separate mkI/mkII/**mkIII** `.umc` wrappers over one `.usp`. The manufacturer treats MK3 as a distinct protocol generation — the same split Extron expresses as two packages, and the reason the 5940 comparison was invalid.

The general lesson: a manufacturer artifact is an **adjudicator**, not just a third opinion. It should be the tiebreaker whenever the generated output and a shipped module disagree.

## 6. Ranked next steps — fix these before pulling more samples

More data cannot fix an overfitted rule set; it can only re-measure it. Everything above the line is a rule fix validated across all six pairs, reporting wire-match *and* dangling every time.

1. **Stop injecting SIS wire strings into non-SIS devices.** `w0echo`/`w3cv` in a Biamp Tesira and a Clock Audio DSP driver is wire-content invention — the failure mode the project is built to avoid — and it is shipping today in two of six outputs. Gate `FIXED_SET_UPDATE_HELPER_SIS_ETHERNET` on SIS evidence in the source script; otherwise carry GC's own helper through the rewriter and raise a residual. Test-first, non-negotiable, highest priority.
2. **Generalise the Emulated pre-write strip** to statement level regardless of guard shape. Expected: dangling 5 → 3 in-sample, 51 → 3 on Biamp, zero wire-table movement. Justified by the shipped modules, and it fixes a latent in-sample bug, not just Biamp's.
3. **Make `wire_table` cover the helper bodies and transport classes**, or add a second metric that does. Both #1 and #4 were invisible to the current scorecard while it reported 85% for Biamp. A metric that cannot see invented wire strings is the most dangerous artifact in the repo.
4. **Fix protocol-asset resolution and fail loudly.** 20 of 23 Biamp models resolve to no protocol asset, a declared `SerialProtocolAsset` is never seen, two of three shipped transport classes are never emitted, and *no residual is raised*. Silence is the bug; emitting the missing transports is the follow-on.
5. **Fix the scorecard's pairing policy.** Report Clock Audio 5940 and Samsung ethernet as "no shipped oracle — unscored", not as percentages. Report in-sample and held-out separately, and report fidelity-to-source alongside agreement-with-shipped, because those are 100% and 83% and conflating them is what produced the "~95%" claim.
6. **Add manufacturer artifacts as a formal adjudication tier.** When generated and shipped disagree, check the vendor's own module before labelling anything. It flipped all three Clock Audio verdicts and found the `SRBG` typo.
7. **Only then pull more samples** — and pull them as *matched pairs* (a .pkp whose model set is confirmed against the shipped module's command set before scoring), ideally with a manufacturer module. A genuine MK3 ControlScript module would make 5940 a real seventh data point.

Not worth doing: chasing the 14 held-out wire differences. Every one is a human edit that postdates generation. Closing them requires guessing, and guessing is worse than the 83%.
